verdict.justification: Both deliverables arrive at the same draft balance due of $15,379 and identify the principal income, credits, and additional taxes, but A provides materially better senior-review risk identification. A recognizes that Lisa's $26,406.43 elective deferral may exceed the applicable limit and explains the possible income adjustment, whereas B incorrectly assures the reviewer that it 'does not change the return.' A also flags the incongruity of a wash-sale loss adjustment on Lisa's profitable sale and recommends broker confirmation; B simply adds the adjustment without identifying that concern. A more faithfully maps Schedule 2 to the 2024 form, while B reverses the AMT and excess advance premium tax credit entries in Part I and misuses line 18 as a total of additional taxes. Both packages remain incomplete as final returns because they defer the potentially beneficial Texas sales-tax deduction and require entry into e-file software, although A states the SALT cap implications more carefully. A does have a notable presentation omission—the individual credit amounts are missing from Schedule 3 lines 1 and 2—but its stronger substantive review guidance makes it the preferable package.
